articles.title_original: Tailoring Cross‐Scale Structures in Dual‐Transition Metal MXene Aerogels for Robust Microwave Absorption
articles.title_en: Tailoring Cross-Scale Structures in Dual-Transition Metal MXene Aerogels for Robust Microwave Absorption
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Achieving broadband microwave absorption while maintaining a thin profile is a challenge due to the conflict of inherent impedance with attenuation. Herein, dual‐transition metal /rGO/ aerogels featuring cross‐scale structural tailoring, ranging from the nanoscale to the millimeter scale, were fabricated via freeze‐drying. At the nanoscale, the solid‐solution incorporation of Nb atoms introduces additional polarization loss, thereby enhancing the intrinsic attenuation capacity of the material. At the microscopic level, by leveraging the dimensional disparity between large‐sheet rGO and small‐sheet MXene, the porosity of the aerogel walls was regulated. Therefore, the conductive networks and abundant heterointerfaces were established, enabling the TNrF‐1 to achieve an effective absorption bandwidth (EAB) of 6.24 GHz at a thickness of 2.0 mm, accompanied by a minimum reflection loss of dB. Macroscopically, the aerogels were constructed into a stepped gradient structure whose parameters were optimized by a genetic algorithm. The optimized architecture reconciles the conflict between impedance and attenuation, delivering an exceptional EAB of 14.45 GHz with superior angular robustness. This cross‐scale paradigm paves a feasible avenue for developing advanced electromagnetic functional materials.
articles.summary_en: Researchers have fabricated dual-transition metal /rGO/ aerogels featuring cross-scale structural tailoring for enhanced broadband microwave absorption. By integrating Nb atoms at the nanoscale and leveraging dimensional disparities between large-sheet rGO and small-sheet MXene, the aerogels achieve an effective absorption bandwidth of 14.45 GHz. This study presents a scalable paradigm for developing advanced electromagnetic functional materials.

articles.title_original: Dual‐Anion‐Vacancy Engineering in MXene: Unlocking Quantum Confinement, Charge Compensation and Shielding Effects for Ultra‐Stable Mg <sup>2+</sup> /Li <sup>+</sup> Ions Storage
articles.title_en: Dual-Anion-Vacancy Engineering in MXene for Advanced Mg2+/Li+ Hybrid Batteries
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Designing cathode materials that can synergistically store ions with significantly different charge densities and ionic radii poses a critical challenge in the ongoing development of Mg 2+ /Li + hybrid batteries (MLHBs). MXene‐based materials with vacancy defects offer promise, yet conventional monovacancy strategies cannot balance capacity and reaction kinetics. Herein, an innovative dual‐anion (Se, O) vacancy engineering strategy is proposed and constructed a quantum dot (QD) Ti 3 C 2 MXene heterostructure (QD@V Se,O ‐Ti 3 C 2 ). Benefiting from (i) the quantum confinement effect induced by QD TiO 2 , which modifies the electronic band structure and improves interfacial charge transfer, (ii) dual‐anion vacancies that establish a complementary charge environment, providing electrostatic shielding to lower Mg 2+ diffusion barriers and facilitate charge compensation, and (iii) in situ formed TiSe 2 layers combined with strong Se─C bonds, which ensure rapid ion/electron transport and maintain structural integrity. The QD@V Se,O ‐Ti 3 C 2 cathode delivers an ultra‐high capacity (705 mAh g −1 at 50 mA g −1 ) and outstanding cycling stability with 70% capacity retention after 2300 cycles at 1000 mA g −1 . The synergy among quantum‐confined, charge compensation and shielding effects, and interfacial electronic structure achieved unprecedented Mg 2+ /Li + co‐adsorption stability and rapid kinetics. This work establishes a new paradigm of QD‐enhanced multi‐anion vacancy engineering for next‐generation multivalent‐ion batteries.
articles.summary_en: Researchers propose an innovative dual-anion vacancy engineering strategy combined with a quantum dot MXene heterostructure to improve hybrid battery performance. The resulting cathode material achieves high capacity and exceptional cycling stability by optimizing charge compensation and quantum confinement effects. This study presents a promising approach for developing next-generation multivalent-ion energy storage systems.

articles.title_original: Terahertz spectroscopy of intrinsic and photoexcited carrier dynamics in Ti 2 CT x MXene films
articles.title_en: Terahertz spectroscopy reveals carrier dynamics in Ti2CTx MXene films
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Metallic MXenes hold strong potential for applications in flexible electronics, electromagnetic interference shielding, photonics, and photothermal energy conversion. Realizing these applications requires a detailed understanding of carrier transport and its response to optical excitation. Here, we use terahertz (THz) time-domain spectroscopy and THz time-resolved spectroscopy to investigate the intrinsic conductivity and ultrafast photoresponse of Ti 2 CT x MXene, a less-explored member of the MXene family. Analysis of the complex THz conductivity spectra suggests that oxidation fragments Ti 2 CT x flakes into small, conductive regions separated by non-conductive areas. Within these conductive regions, electrons exhibit scattering times and local mobilities comparable to those in Ti 3 C 2 T x . These mobilities represent intrinsic upper limits that could be realized in Ti 2 CT x at macroscopic scales with improved oxidative stability and processing. Photoexcitation at both 400 nm and 800 nm induces a transient enhancement in THz conductivity, in contrast to Ti 3 C 2 T x , where photothermal heating suppresses mobility. Most photoexcited carriers in Ti 2 CT x recombine or become trapped within a few picoseconds, while a small fraction persists for hundreds of picoseconds. Photoinduced carriers exhibit longer scattering times and reduced localization compared to intrinsic carriers, suggesting that their excess kinetic energy allows them to overcome barriers from defects and oxidation. Excitation wavelength influences early-time dynamics: 800 nm excitation results in a slower rise and decay than 400 nm, consistent with inter-valley scattering between conduction-band valleys of differing mobility, or with initial excitation into low-mobility, defect-associated sta
articles.summary_en: Researchers utilize terahertz time-domain and time-resolved spectroscopy to investigate the intrinsic conductivity and ultrafast photoresponse of Ti2CTx MXene films. The analysis shows that oxidation fragments the flakes into small conductive regions separated by non-conductive areas, while photoexcitation induces a transient enhancement in THz conductivity. These findings provide critical insights into carrier transport and scattering mechanisms for potential applications in photonics and flexible electronics.

articles.title_original: Interface Engineering of Boron Nitride–Polymer Composites for High Thermal Conductivity
articles.title_en: Interface Engineering of Boron Nitride-Polymer Composites for High Thermal Conductivity
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT With the rapid miniaturisation and integration of electronic devices, efficient thermal management has become critically important. Boron nitride (BN)‐polymer composites have attracted extensive attention owing to their high thermal conductivity and electrical insulation properties. However, the interfacial thermal resistance between BN and the polymer matrix limits their performance. Consequently, overcoming this bottleneck through interface engineering has emerged as a key research focus. This review systematically examines the current progress in BN‐polymer composites from the perspective of interface engineering. First, the phonon‐mediated heat transfer mechanism and the bottleneck of interfacial thermal resistance are analyzed. Subsequently, various interface engineering strategies are classified according to the forms of interfacial interaction between BN and the polymer. These strategies include covalent bonding, non‐covalent interactions, and physical morphology control. In addition, defect engineering is discussed as an emerging perspective, offering insights into interface design. The effectiveness of the above strategies in establishing continuous thermal conduction pathways and enhancing the performance of the composites is evaluated. Finally, application prospects are summarized and future research directions are proposed.
articles.summary_en: This academic review examines recent advances in interface engineering for boron nitride-polymer composites to improve thermal conductivity and address high interfacial thermal resistance. It details strategies such as covalent bonding, non-covalent interactions, physical morphology control, and defect engineering to optimize phonon-mediated heat transfer for electronic device applications. The findings offer valuable pathways for designing high-performance thermally conductive composite materials.

articles.title_original: Mixed convection and entropy generation in an open cavity for thermal control applications using GO + MXene hybrid nanofluids and phase change material
articles.title_en: Mixed Convection and Entropy Generation in Thermal Control Open Cavities Using GO and MXene Hybrid Nanofluids
articles.excerpt_original: Purpose The primary purpose of this study is to investigate the mixed convection and entropy generation performance of an open cavity using a combination of phase change materials (PCM), metal foam and hybrid nanofluids (HyNFs). By evaluating various cavity orientations, PCM layer thicknesses and nanoparticle concentrations under different flow conditions, the research aims to identify the optimal configuration for uniform heat distribution. Ultimately, the study seeks to provide an effective and innovative thermal control perspective for optimizing heat generation systems. Design/methodology/approach A numerical approach was used to analyze an open cavity integrating a PCM, metal foam and GO + MXene hybrid nanofluids. Computations were performed under laminar flow conditions (Re = 100 and 1,000) with a constant heat flux of 1,000 W/m² applied to all cases. The study systematically evaluated three different cavity orientations, two PCM layer thicknesses (0.2D and 0.5D), and varying nanoparticle weight concentrations (0.1, 0.2 and 0.3 Wt.%) to assess their combined effects on mixed convection, melting performance and entropy generation. Findings The results demonstrate that the vertical upper cavity orientation is optimal for uniform heat distribution, reaching steady state significantly faster (1,200 s earlier) than the horizontal setup. Notably, adding nanoparticles suppressed natural convection, which decreased melting performance. However, the highest Nusselt number (Nu) was achieved using 0.3 Wt.% hybrid nanofluid across all conditions, with the vertical upper cavity doubling the Nu compared to other configurations. articles.summary_en: This academic study numerically investigates the mixed convection and entropy generation performance of an open cavity integrating phase change materials, metal foam, and GO plus MXene hybrid nanofluids. The findings indicate that vertical upper cavity orientations optimize uniform heat distribution and enhance the Nusselt number, whereas nanoparticle additions can suppress natural convection. The research provides insights for optimizing advanced thermal management and heat generation systems.
